title: Delta Adds Philadelphia From LAX, Boosts Flights to Seven More Cities
excerpt: The Atlanta-based carrier will launch a daily LAX–Philadelphia nonstop in June 2027 and add frequencies on seven existing routes, building its largest-ever Los Angeles schedule as the hub battle with United and American intensifies.
body:
• Delta will launch a new daily nonstop between Los Angeles and Philadelphia on June 7, 2027, operated with an Airbus A321neo.
  • The announcement follows a new LAX–Monterey route starting December 19, 2026 — Delta's return to California's Central Coast after a 19-year hiatus.
  • Beginning next spring, Delta will add daily frequencies on seven existing LAX routes: Boston, Cincinnati, Houston, Raleigh, San Antonio, San Diego and Seattle.
  • At its summer 2027 peak, Delta plans more than 200 daily departures to nearly 70 destinations from LAX — the largest schedule it has ever operated there.

Delta Air Lines announced Friday a new nonstop route from Los Angeles International Airport to Philadelphia, plus additional daily flights on seven existing routes — the carrier's second LAX expansion in less than a week, and the clearest signal yet of its ambitions in one of America's most contested aviation markets.

Philadelphia joins the LAX network

The new daily flight to Philadelphia International Airport will launch June 7, 2027, aboard an Airbus A321neo. It is a strategically pointed addition: American Airlines is currently the only carrier flying nonstop between LAX and Philadelphia, with six to eight daily departures, and Philadelphia functions as American's principal transatlantic gateway. Delta's single daily flight will not match American's frequency, but it fills a conspicuous hole for Los Angeles-based Delta loyalists and passengers connecting through SkyTeam partners at LAX.

Monterey and the California buildup

The Philadelphia news arrived just days after Delta unveiled a return to Monterey on California's Central Coast, where it will fly twice daily from LAX beginning December 19, 2026, with Delta Connection Embraer 175s — ending a 19-year absence. Daily service from Salt Lake City to Monterey starts the same day. "We're creating more opportunities for customers to connect to the places they want to go while building on our long-term commitment to Los Angeles and the West," said Amy Martin, Delta's vice president of network planning.

Seven routes, more frequencies

Starting next spring, Delta will add daily flights across seven existing LAX markets: Raleigh-Durham rises to two daily flights on April 12, Boston to five on May 6, San Diego to five on June 7, and Seattle to eight, Cincinnati to two, and Houston and San Antonio to three each on July 11. All told, Delta expects to fly its biggest schedule ever in Los Angeles next year, with more than 200 peak-day departures to nearly 70 destinations at the summer 2027 peak.

The hub battle heats up

Los Angeles remains one of the fiercest battlegrounds in US aviation, with Delta, American and United each operating a hub at LAX. Cirium data shows Delta already leading in 2025 with 53,600 departures and 8.6 million scheduled seats, ahead of United's 49,000 departures and American's 48,000. But United holds a bigger Pacific schedule from the airport and will grow its long-haul offerings in 2027 with new service to Osaka.

"It's a very competitive marketplace, and we're in it to win it as well. But I suspect it will be very competitive for the foreseeable future."

— Andrew Nocella, United chief commercial officer

Delta is backing its claim as Los Angeles' leading carrier with hardware: a newly opened second Delta One Lounge at LAX, long-haul launches to Hong Kong and Melbourne since last winter, a Manila route announced in July, and Vancouver service returning in November for the first time in eight years.

What it means for travelers

For Southern California's large Indian-American community — one of the biggest in the United States — the expansion means more domestic feed into LAX, strengthening connections to Delta's growing transpacific network and its SkyTeam partners. More seats on competitive routes also tends to mean more fare choices, a welcome development for families planning trips to India that route through LAX gateways.

What's next

Watch for a response: United and American are unlikely to cede Los Angeles quietly, and Delta executives have made clear that Asia is where they see the most growth opportunity. The airline's next LAX announcements may well point west across the Pacific.
